title: Fourth Annual Indian Food Festival Returns to Colorado Springs on August 1

body:
The Fourth Annual Indian Food Festival is returning to Colorado Springs on Saturday, August 1, promising an afternoon of authentic Indian cuisine, cultural performances, and community celebration at Liberty High School. Organized by Polka Dots and Curry, the free-admission event has grown into one of the region's most anticipated cultural gatherings, drawing hundreds of food enthusiasts and families from across the Front Range.

A Feast for the Senses

Running from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. at Liberty High School on Scarborough Drive, the festival offers a full immersion into Indian culinary and cultural traditions. Attendees can expect a wide variety of dishes spanning India's diverse regional cuisines, from rich curries and biryanis to street food favorites and sweet desserts.

But the festival extends well beyond food. The organizers have lined up a packed program that includes traditional Indian dance performances, live music, Bollywood dance classes for all skill levels, and professional henna artists offering intricate mehndi designs. A cultural performance program on the main stage is scheduled from 1 to 2 p.m., highlighted by a saree fashion walk at 1:30 p.m.

Vendors selling Indian clothing, jewelry, and other products from local family-owned businesses will also be on hand, along with raffle and contest prizes throughout the afternoon.

Growing Community Celebration

What started as a modest neighborhood gathering has blossomed into a signature event for Colorado Springs' Indian community. Polka Dots and Curry, the organization behind the festival, has steadily built its following, with nearly 200 followers on its event pages and growing attendance year over year.

General admission is free starting at noon, though pre-registration is required to help food vendors plan for demand. An early access option is available for those who want to beat the crowds, offering entry at 11 a.m. along with a raffle entry and a free Indian e-cookbook download. The venue provides free parking in its large school lot.

Indian Culture Thriving in the Mountain West

The festival reflects the growing vitality of Indian diaspora communities in smaller American cities beyond the traditional coastal hubs. Colorado Springs, home to a steadily expanding South Asian population, has seen increasing demand for Indian cultural programming and cuisine in recent years.

For Indian Americans in the Pikes Peak region, events like the food festival serve as vital touchpoints for cultural preservation and community building. They also offer non-Indian residents an accessible gateway into one of the world's richest culinary traditions.

"Whether you're a foodie or just looking to try something new, this festival is the place to be," the organizers say on the event page. Sponsorship inquiries can be directed to indianfoodfestcolorado@gmail.com, and more information is available at indianfoodfestival.co.

The Fourth Annual Indian Food Festival takes place Saturday, August 1, at Liberty High School, 8720 Scarborough Drive, Colorado Springs, CO 80920.
